Apple Watch SE 3 vs Series 12: Which should you buy this holiday season?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift.
  • The Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem.
  • It has been revealed that the Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift. Apple’s lineup includes the affordable Apple Watch SE 3 and the more advanced Apple Watch Series 12.

Here’s how those two Apple Watch models stack up….

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem. It got a big upgrade last year, adding a variety of new higher-end Apple Watch features. It now offers an Always-On display, sleep apnea notifications, temperature sensing, interactive wrist flick and double tap gestures, and more.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode. It supports fast charging, going from 0-80% in 45 minutes.

Even though it hasn’t been updated in a year, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a very compelling option, especially for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem. It’s pretty fantastic that you can get an Apple Watch with key display and health-monitoring features for under $200.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s newest smartwatch, and it’s a significant update over its predecessor. This year, Apple doubled down on the health and fitness capabilities of Apple Watch with an all-new Health Sensing System.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the manufacturer conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”.

According to recent reports, with the latest system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

As I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The newly introduced sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

Recent findings suggest that the Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

What do you think of the current Apple Watch lineup? Are you shopping for one this holiday season? Let us know down in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents.
  • “That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic states.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that anthropic is launching a upcoming tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”.

In a recent development, claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

“That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic states. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic states.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the newly introduced /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic notes.

Industry observers note that you can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

Introducing Claude Ship (beta): Claude can review your pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones your team's policy allows.The goal is to help you ship code as fast as you can write it. pic.twitter.com/b9OBAhEBmr.

  • According to recent reports, the iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

Sources indicate that that's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

According to recent reports, the iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

In a recent development, the iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Industry observers note that apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

Sources indicate that the only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for people who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee plans to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sources indicate that sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

In a recent development, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Yes, Apple participates in Cyber Monday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

This summer Apple TV aired the highly anticipated return of Ted Lasso.

Season 4 debuted three full years after the last season ended, and brought a fresh start to one of the streamer’s all-time most beloved series.

But after the season 4 finale aired, Apple provided no indication whether the show would continue or not.

Now, uncertainty around the show’s fate is over.

Apple has declared that Ted Lasso season 5 is officially coming.

Following its hit fourth season, Apple’s global phenomenon “Ted Lasso” is officially returning back to the pitch for season five. Starring and executive produced by Emmy Award winner Jason Sudeikis, the fourth season of “Ted Lasso” introduced the Lady Greyhounds, with critics hailing it as “a perfect setup for a fresh return” and “one of the most beloved comedy highlights of the decade.”.

It has been revealed that the announcement is light on further details. However, there should be a much shorter wait for season 5 than there was for season 4.

According to recent reports, before Ted Lasso returned this year, Jason Sudeikis shared that he had a latest three-season arc in mind. Apple’s Eddy Cue also suggested the company would be happy to continue making more seasons for years to come.

But until today’s announcement, the lack of official news still put Lasso fans’ hopes on pause.

Whether it returns in 2027 or, perhaps more likely 2028, Ted Lasso isn’t going away again anytime soon.

It has been revealed that are you excited for Ted Lasso’s season 5 renewal? Let us know in the comments.

Offering support for iPhone and Android’s tracking networks, the newly introduced Kodak SlideTag offers the neat added functionality over an AirTag of being able to show your photos and more on an E-Ink display.

The Kodak SlideTag is inspired by classic 35mm slides from Kodak cameras, and is built by the same manufacturer, Reto, that released a keychain digital camera inspired by old Kodak cameras too. The tracker’s E-Ink display is designed mainly to showcase your photos, with storage built-in for up to 12 photos, but also the ability to show lists and QR codes.

The SlideTag’s extra features are controlled by the Kodak Memory Link app, while tracking is handled in the Find My app on iPhone just like an AirTag (and the Find Hub app on Android phones).

There are nine total styles for the SlideTag, all sold in a blind box format. You can order one tracker for $35 with the whole set also available for purchase.

Eight of the styles have a one-in-eight chance of finding, while the ninth style is only found in one out of every 64 boxes.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there is arguably no better day for football — watching it or playing it — than the autumnal crispness of Thanksgiving. But on this particular late summer afternoon, despite triple-digit temperatures and the Oklahoma sun making it feel even hotter, football is the sweat-drenched task at hand: Coach Kyle Ross is putting me through practice. It’s not lost on either of us that Ross’s primary job is coaching high-energy junior-high athletes in the state’s flagship football program, at Bixby, and I’m an out-of-shape journalist in his late 40s. If I finish Ross’s drills upright and healthy, we’ll declare it a success.

“What are you? Three-for-three or four-for-four catching passes here?” Ross — who is also the founder and frontman of the band Keyland — asks me. My football career ended in high school, 30 years ago, but I was a slot receiver with a reputation for catching anything thrown my way. What would my parents say if I started dropping passes now? “I will throw my body on this turf to not miss a pass,” I promise him.

Over the next few months, Ross will attempt to strike a rather unique balance as coach and touring artist. He’ll headline and sell out the Mercury Lounge in Tulsa, 30 minutes north of Bixby, open an East Coast run for Morgan Wade, and announce a series of 2027 dates supporting Kaitlin Butts. And while he’s ostensibly promoting Knuckle Sandwich, Keyland’s third studio album, Ross will always have football season in the back of his mind.

It has been revealed that “I haven’t found anything better to do,” Ross claims of why he continues to coach. “Except for maybe, get paid to play guitar and drink beer.”.

Recent findings suggest that few pastimes are as all-encompassing in Oklahoma as football. Its two largest college programs — Oklahoma and Oklahoma State — play their home games in modern stadiums to sold-out crowds on most Saturdays in the fall, but it’s the high-school version of the sport that unites the state. Students, fans, and parents fill stadiums in the state’s urban cores and rural farm towns every Friday night, and for the past decade, no program has dominated this landscape like Bixby’s. The varsity Spartans are eight-time defending champions in Oklahoma’s largest class and this season were ranked No. 1 again by the state’s largest media outlet. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

This is Ross’s program. He’s an assistant coach for Bixby’s eighth-grade team and a junior-high English teacher. He grew up in rural Missouri, playing football through high school. Shortly after graduating college, Ross befriended Tyler Schneider — Bixby’s longtime offensive coordinator. The two hit it off, and within weeks, Ross joined the Spartan’s staff. Seven years later, Ross is throwing passes to me on the same turf that those Spartans play their home games. We’re here to talk about music, but I am here to experience what it’s like being one of Ross’s players.

Industry observers note that “Let’s go!” he shouts as I haul in another pass. “And he scores!”.

Recent findings suggest that as it happens, that particular end zone is where I scored my last touchdown as a player. Before Bixby became the state’s juggernaut program, it was a mid-sized school in the same conference as my hometown team, the Okmulgee Bulldogs.

When he’s playing as Keyland — Ross uses the moniker interchangeably for his solo and full-band highlights, named for a duck club he and his father used to hunt near his Chillicothe, Missouri, hometown — he wears an infectious smile that’s integral to his show. He describes the irreverent Knuckle Sandwich, which Keyland recorded at the Sonic Ranch studio outside of El Paso, as a product of pals hanging around for several days and finding music at the end of it. Related Content Jason Scott and the High Heat Are the Cool, If Raunchy, Band Americana Music Needs Honky-Tonk Woman: Kaitlin Butts Is As Ambitious As She Wants to Be You’ve Been Streaming ‘Broken Window Serenade.’ This Is the Texas Band Who Wrote It Wade Bowen Is Texas Music.

Recent findings suggest that “This album is about taking what you do seriously, but not taking yourself seriously,” Ross states. “That kind of embodies the whole creative process in recording it. It’s more of a hang than anything, and we get music at the end of it.”.

It’s a microcosm for his entire music career. He had a guitar growing up, but played it sparingly. It was not until he was in college and caught a Chris Stapleton gig that he decided to give music a try. “I fell in love with Chris Stapleton, and that was the entry way to the long rabbit hole I fell into,” he says.

Sources indicate that landing a full-time job right in the heart of Tulsa’s music community was a bout of good fortune. Ross befriended Brandon Clark, frontman of the Red Dirt outfit BC & the Major Rig and highly respected in Red Dirt circles. Clark has a weekly gig at Mercury Lounge, and in 2022, he suggested that Keyland get booked at the bar.

Keyland’s first Mercury Lounge show was opening for the Substantial Rig. Shortly afterward, venue general manager Ashley Kirkley booked Keyland as a headliner. The show sold out, and Keyland have been a regular since.

“Keyland is a great band, no doubt, but the energy and charisma that emanates from Kyle is palpable at every show,” Kirkley notes. “Beyond being an incredible performer with a distinctive voice that is unlike anything I’ve heard, he is also one of the most down to earth, kindest people I have ever met. Kyle is always striving for greatness in everything he does. He’s an incredible human, and we are incredibly lucky to have him as a part of our music family.”.

Industry observers note that keyland have since gone on to, at least, regional notoriety. Ross has been booked multiple times at nearby Cain’s Ballroom, playing alongside the likes of Johnny Mullenax and opening a sold-out show for Josh Abbott earlier this year.

“Everyone’s at different levels of what they’re doing,” Ross notes of the Tulsa music community. “I have friends who have sold out a place like Cain’s. I’m friends with people who are doing house highlights for ten people. It almost seems like everyone has a very similar mindset of, ‘We’re almost there.’”.

In a recent development, ross knows better than anyone that Keyland is growing at a fast clip. He is likely to come to a crossroads between coaching and making music before too many more gigs or summer practices pass. But until then, he’s happy to pull double duty. And even at Bixby, where the focus is annually on another state championship, he has found support. He had a fan from the start in Schneider, but he’s brought most of the Spartans’ coaching staff onto his bandwagon — and even a few players.

Sources indicate that “There’s a huge Venn diagram of coaches’ interests outside of football, and one of them is music,” Ross claims. “All the coaches are super supportive. We have over 20 coaches, and a huge number of them have been to more than one concert. It’s just a community-oriented place to work. The kids, as they get older, they start to appreciate it.”.

It has been revealed that and on that note, practice is over. Ross’s actual players are starting to trickle in to Bixby’s behemoth of a training facility. Ross gives me a Bixby Spartans shirt for surviving his drills. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

In a recent development, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully released on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Industry observers note that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Recent findings suggest that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX released on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a newly introduced rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

Sources indicate that if all goes according to blueprint, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” indicates Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

In a recent development, once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to proposal, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” states Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

Recent findings suggest that the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Industry observers note that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu indicates, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

In a recent development, idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” indicates Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

Recent findings suggest that A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” notes Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she notes. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Sources indicate that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday indicates.

According to recent reports, despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday states Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Industry observers note that idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec claims. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel states the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

Sources indicate that the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

It has been revealed that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel indicates. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu indicates.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel indicates. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

According to recent reports, “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with fresh customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube update.

Recent findings suggest that in the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app rolled out on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

According to recent reports, android Authority spotted several fresh app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta update (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow users to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

That noted, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

In a recent development, nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Black Friday, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which launched in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the firm’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

Recent findings suggest that that said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  Nov. 30, 2026. #131432. All the ‘GTA’ Games Ever, Ranked

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3270 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollingstone ↗ Open Full Page

All the ‘GTA’ Games Ever, Ranked

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3270 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, unless you’ve been locked in a bank vault somewhere for the last 30 years, there’s a good chance that you’ve heard of Grand Theft Auto.
  • But more so than the money, GTA’s influence on gaming and culture at large is its true legacy.
  • Outside of the industry sphere, GTA became a touchstone for gaming as a concept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, unless you’ve been locked in a bank vault somewhere for the last 30 years, there’s a good chance that you’ve heard of Grand Theft Auto. Originally released for PC and PlayStation in 1997, the series began as a solid commercial success for fans of edgy humor and shooters, before becoming a pop culture phenomenon in the early 2000s. Today, it’s one of the most recognizable entertainment properties on Earth, transcending the boundaries of just gaming — with its latest iteration, GTA VI, arriving this year with the highest grossing media launch ever. Day one sales of GTA VI generated over $3.79 billion, more than any other game or movie, amounting to the GDP of a small nation.

But more so than the money, GTA’s influence on gaming and culture at large is its true legacy. The open-world crime saga has informed the way video games are developed; its cinematic tone nailed an old Hollywood flavor that earlier games could only vaguely emulate; the freedom of choice in how to play inspired imitators of all kinds, from kid-friendly fare to direct copycats chasing the violent gangster gameplay.

Outside of the industry sphere, GTA became a touchstone for gaming as a concept. Think of any movie or show where characters are playing video games; it’s very likely the visual depiction will be a crudely rendered clone of GTA. A target of endless pearlclutching, politicians and advocates on both sides of the aisle have paraded the name as a leading cause of societal decay. To some, it’s a hedonistic simulacrum of sex and violence, encouraging players to indulge their darkest impulses.

And, sure, it’s a series where you can assault sex workers and commit mass shootings, but those options bely the point of Grand Theft Auto as a whole. At their best, the games serve as an intricately written parody of American culture — the greed, hypocrisy, and often downright idiocy that the country wears so proudly. In GTA, the American Dream is something to be gripped by force, and is delivered to audiences through caricature. It takes all the stories, media, and norms we love and reflects them back as satire. GTA doesn’t glorify crime, people do. It’s just laughing at us along the way.

To that end, not every GTA is so successful. The early top-down entries served more as arcade-style run-and-gunners that did little to admonish players to think beyond wanton destruction. But as technology evolved and storytelling devices matured, GTA began to better embody its role as Mean Streets meets South Park, telling exaggerated tales of criminality gone wrong to make audiences flinch — at least momentarily, before plotting their next heist.

Sources indicate that in honor of GTA VI’s long-awaited release, Rolling Stone is ranking every Grand Theft Auto, from their humble Nineties-era origins to the modern blockbusters, both main games and expansions. Here’s every one, from worst to best.

It has been revealed that although the first two games in the series made appearances on the Game Boy Color, Grand Theft Auto Advance was the first original entry specifically developed for a Nintendo device. Blending the top-down overhead perspective of the OG installments with the mission structure of then-ubiquitous 3D versions, GTA Advance bridges the series’ oft-forgotten older design with more accessible gameplay.

Recent findings suggest that as a prequel to 2001’s GTA III, players control a low-rent criminal named Mike whose dream of leaving Liberty City behind is blown to shreds by the mafia. Storywise, the plot comes through mostly via text and isn’t much to cling to. The handheld hardware of the Game Boy Advance doesn’t allow for much graphical fidelity, resulting in a game that looks worse than even the first PC entry, but is still commendable as a pocket-friendly way to play GTA.

To capitalize on the success of the original game, two expansions were green-lit as interim teasers before 1999’s full-fledged sequel. Grand Theft Auto: London 1969 released earlier that year as a standalone purchase, with 1961 following suit as a free download. Neither entry was groundbreaking, mostly recycling the gameplay and visuals of the base game with a Swingin’ Sixties finish. The duology is mostly fascinating for being the only GTA games set in a real city rather than fictional versions of American locales. The setting did result in one major innovation, however, with licensed music introduced to the franchise for the in-game radio stations — a feature that would become an essential part of GTA’s appeal moving forward.

In a recent development, looking back, it’s hard to imagine how a game as simple as the original Grand Theft Auto kickstarted a media dynasty. Developed by Scottish studio DMA Design (now Rockstar North), the initial concept began as a simple cops and robbers sim called Race ‘n’ Chase, before being overhauled to focus on the more open-ended crime-oriented mission structure. Players choose from an assortment of unnamed protagonists to control, and must complete six linear levels spread across three cities (Liberty City, San Andreas, and Vice City), accruing a set number of points to progress.

Although seemingly basic in its top-down design, with a world composed mostly of tiny dot-like people and a handful of vehicle options, the first GTA built the foundation for everything else to come. Its six levels each serve as small sandboxes where players can choose to score cash as they see fit, and each city would later be fleshed out as fully realized urban sprawls in the 3D games. Like any of the series’ main characters, this freshman outing represents a humble start with great aspirations.

While the first batch of Game Boy Color and Advance releases proved that the series’ formula could be replicated for handheld with a few concessions, Liberty City Stories took things a step further — bringing a fully 3D GTA to the PlayStation Portable. Like GTA Advance, this all-new entry serves as a prequel to GTA III, albeit much more faithfully rendered, with graphics matching the home console version and even fully recorded voice acting for its cinematic cut scenes. In fact, it’s superior in some ways, incorporating gameplay features like changeable clothing and more intuitive camera controls. Once ported to the PlayStation 2, the game’s cracks began to show slightly; it’s a mostly inessential side quest for those who want more GTA III. But, in its initial portable incarnation, Liberty City Stories is a technical marvel.

The second spinoff developed for PlayStation Portable, Vice City Stories is yet another shining example of the impressive capabilities of Sony’s first foray into the handheld market. A prequel to 2002’s Vice City, it carries over the Eighties setting and includes an impressive voice cast for what’s essentially a mobile game, including Gary Busey, Miami Vice star Philip Michael Thomas, and even Phil Collins as himself.

Unlike its PSP predecessor, Vice City Stories does more than just replicate the console experience on-the-go, introducing some very ambitious new mechanics to the experience. The most prominent is the concept of empire building, where players must topple local local gang-affiliated businesses, then usurp control to create a network of private income sources, from brothels to protection rackets. Also like the previous game, Vice City Stories features a six-person multiplayer mode, although that feature was removed for the later PlayStation 2 rerelease.

Sources indicate that while GTA as a series frequently pivots between settings and perspectives, Chinatown Wars marks some of the biggest departures for the franchise’s look and gameplay overall. The handheld game blends the top-down view of the early titles with a newly introduced cel-shaded aesthetic with thick character and environmental outlines reminiscent of a comic book. Initially designed for the dual-screen Nintendo DS, its gameplay features numerous touchscreen-based minigames — although both these controls and the stylized visuals were swapped out for the later PSP release.

In a recent development, but the most notable change in Chinatown Wars is a greater emphasis on drug-dealing, something that was controversial at release. As a Triad member, players can sell heroin, ecstasy, weed, cocaine and more — as well as strategize around different market conditions and geographical supply. It’s a murky system that goes deeper than most games in the series, which mostly ask the user to smuggle narcotics rather than peddle them directly.

At launch, GTA 2 was met with a mixed reception, mostly for failing to meaningfully innovate beyond the first game’s premise and design. But that’s not entirely true. The 1997 original did well to introduce the basics of open-ended mission structure and player choice, but its sequel perfected the formula for the pseudo-2D era.

Set in a fictional retro-futuristic city called Anywhere, U.S.A., GTA 2 sees players once again controlling a itty bitty protagonist as they conduct crime in a sequence of missions to progress through each level. This time, the setting is one large city divided by districts, and features rival gangs to work for, each at odds with each other. Balancing favor between the syndicates is key, and an increased level of environmental interactivity can lead to gang members engaging in their own immersive firefights with the police and each other. GTA 2 isn’t quite the quantum leap forward that its successor would be, but it’s a delightful piece of retro gaming nostalgia whose DNA can be seen in later indie games like Hotline Miami (2012).

Recent findings suggest that before the turn of the millennium, the GTA series had been a modest success, selling millions of units on PC and PlayStation, but it hadn’t quite hit the zeitgeist. GTA III would be the beginning of the dominant cultural force we know today. Rebooting the series’ narrative into a latest continuity moving forward, it once again drops players into the New York-inspired setting of Liberty City — now rendered in full 3D — for an exponentially more cinematic experience.

It has been revealed that for gamers, GTA III is a foundational text, popularizing many design choices and mechanics today’s player take for granted. Its urban open-world feels lived in, peppered with cars and pedestrians, each on their own loop that can be upended. Combat and gunplay, while simplistic by modern standards, are deeper than ever before thanks to the 3D leap; the ability to simultaneously drive a car and aim over-the-shoulder for a drive-by was astounding at the time. Most importantly, the first entry of this newly introduced era allowed Rockstar to fully realize the cinematic scope of what Grand Theft Auto always wanted to be. With elaborate cut scenes and voice acting from stars Frank Vincent, Debi Mazar, and Kyle MacLachlan, GTA III pioneered the blurring of lines between games and cinema. It’s basically gaming’s Mean Streets, a New Hollywood crime caper from which generations of developers would borrow from moving forward.

Industry observers note that much like the original game, 2008’s GTA IV received a duology of expansions that built on the base game’s foundation. But unlike the London content, The Lost and the Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony substantially add to the narrative and mechanics of their progenitor beyond being simple reskins.

In a recent development, each expansion follows characters whose stories overlap with the main plot of GTA IV: biker Johnny Klebitz in the TLATD and bodyguard Luis Fernando Lopez in TBOGT. While both play similarly, each has distinct features beyond the base game. Johnny’s motorcycle club plays a huge role in his content, allowing players to call in the gang for backup when things get hairy. Luis’ gameplay isn’t notably different, but the story in his expansion is one of the very best in the series, celebrated at the time for its depiction of LGBTQ characters.

Recent findings suggest that there was a time when game development was a much speedier process, with studios rapidly churning out quality sequels near annually. Rockstar themselves had a generational run from 2001 to 2004, dominating the conversation with the trifecta of GTA III, Vice City, and San Andreas. Even more impressive is how each game substantially improved on its predecessor despite wildly shifting apart in setting and tone.

According to recent reports, vice City falls squarely in the middle of the pack, transposing GTA III’s groundbreaking design into a Miami Vice and Scarface-inspired Eighties crime caper, complete with a lead character voiced by actor Ray Liotta. Control-wise, it’s not a huge leap forward; players still roam an open world hopping between main missions, side quests, and mini-games. What elevates Vice City is its pitch perfect take on Eighties Miami, depicting a greasy city soaked in neon, all set to one of the greatest video game soundtracks of all time.

Until very recently, GTA V was the series’ most ambitious entry to date. For many, it’s the definitive Grand Theft Auto experience — if only by default. The sole franchise entry in 13 years, GTA V was released for PlayStation 3, 4, and 5, selling a ludicrous 230 million copies over the course of its elongated lifespan.

According to recent reports, in many ways, GTA V plays like a greatest hits of the series’ many ideas and mechanics, while modernizing its gameplay just enough to feel like an improvement over IV. Set in the fictional state of San Andreas (although set in a different “universe” than the 2004 title of that name), the story follows three unique protagonists, all with conflicting personalities and motives. Players will bounce between bank robber Michael De Santa, gangster Franklin Clinton, and psychopathic gunrunner Trevor Philips; their interwoven narrative bringing a slightly meandering Tarantino vibe to the otherwise kinetic plot, heavily inspired by Michael Mann’s Heat. Fans would be right to argue that GTA V deserves the top spot based on popularity alone, but looking back on the actual gameplay, it did little to substantially innovate over its direct predecessor. In 2013, GTA V’s gameplay arrived feeling dated, but was bolstered significantly by its feeling of limitless freedom and well-executed campaign story.

It has been revealed that although the series has many flavors, there’s a semblance of homogeny among the distinct crime syndicates throughout GTA. Regardless of the time period, there’s usually a depiction of the Italian mafia, Chinese Triads, maybe some Russians — with some depiction of Cuban and Haitian gangs cropping up in Vice City. 2004’s San Andreas broke served as a massive departure, centering on SoCal gang violence inspired by the Bloods and Crips.

While so much of the franchise’s inspiration seemingly comes from TV and movies (what better societal reflection, after all), San Andreas feels more informed by actual history, weaving in elements of real-life urban crises like the Nineties crack epidemic and the 1992 L.A. riots alongside storytelling lifted from films like John Singleton’s Boyz n the Hood. Outside of its unique setting and more impactful storytelling, one of San Andreas’ greatest contributions is an increased emphasis on the slice-of-life details and mini-games that shape the player character directly — something that is heavily prevalent in this year’s upcoming entry, GTA VI.

Industry observers note that following a legendary run from 2001 to 2006, wherein five 3D GTA releases dominated home consoles and handhelds alike, the expectations for the next numbered entry in the franchise hit a fever pitch in 2008. Fortunately, GTA IV delivered the goods.

Recent findings suggest that resetting the table once again with a fresh vision of Liberty City, GTA IV traded in the sprawling map of San Andreas for a more densely packed and lively version of the series’ original locale. The story also eschewed any direct cinematic parallels to focus on a more original story leaning deeper into the satirical commentary of U.S. culture — specifically the American Dream. Unlike the thuggish mafioso types of games prior, GTA IV’s lead, Niko Bellic, is an ex-soldier and Eastern European immigrant, arriving in the states equally interested in revenge and a fresh start in the land of opportunity. Bringing in an outsider lends the game’s tone a sharper edge; this America is an alien place filled with unserious people.

Sources indicate that although its 2013 follow-up would offer better graphics and more features, GTA IV is essentially a perfected vision of what the 1997 original aimed to be, and stands less on the shoulders of other media to define its voice. This is the game that gave us Grand Theft Auto as we know it today.

Industry observers note that for all its many elements, the defining feature of Grand Theft Auto as an idea is the emphasis on player freedom. Go anywhere, do whatever you want — that’s the ultimate promise. Except, every GTA is bound by the needs of a linear narrative. There’s a story to tell, players are just a part of it. But what if the story was entirely your own?

Industry observers note that GTA Online launched as a 30-player online sandbox that emulated the mission structure of the base game while opening the door to infinite chaos. Rather than chasing down CPU-scripted non-playable characters, owners are suddenly even squared against other humans who can react strategically (or erratically), turning the meta-gameplay of GTA to a new level without the constraints of a campaign story. But storytelling is still key, and following the game’s PC launch in 2015, modders cracked open GTA Online’s world with limitless potential. Now, it’s a platform where online roleplay reigns supreme, a second-life simulator where people go about their daily routines under fictional personas.

In a recent development, on streaming platforms, content creators have turned GTA RP into everything from reality TV to serial killer soap operas. It’s transcended individual gameplay to become its own ever-present world of entertainment to control or passively watch. While GTA V has kept selling throughout console generations, it’s clear that GTA Online has been the lifeblood of the series in its interim time between installments, and racked up billions in revenue that’s funded the series’ next major phase.

There are certain moments in time when a game changes everything. Pong had families enraptured around their cathode ray TVs; Tetris locked people into their screens on-the-go decades before smart phones became the norm. As a series, Grand Theft Auto’s had its fair share of these moments. GTA III stunned gamers with its open world, and V made it feel like it was possible live within a movie.

Sources indicate that GTA VI might be the most incredible feat that Rockstar’s ever executed. From its opening moments, it’s instantly clear that there’s some insane technical alchemy going on. Its characters and environments are near photorealistic, and its world brimming with life. You can touch or do just about anything. In fact, players will spend their first few hours simply making coffee and painting their house.

But beyond the flashy graphics and complex coding of NPC and environmental scripts, the most immediate difference in GTA VI is how mature it feels — and not in the adults-only content kind of way. Its dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, aren’t jade caricatures of criminals pulled from pop media, but instead richly humanized characters with hopes and dreams. Although the game has all the hallmarks of a Grand Theft Auto underworld story, every written beat and player action serves to inform how the relationship between its leads blossoms. Arriving in 2026 to an American culture that’s well beyond parody, Rockstar’s decision to ground its story in the perspective of genuine people elevates it beyond anything the franchise was ever intended to be. GTA VI perfectly encompasses all that excess that Grand Theft Auto should have, while adding in a soul we never knew it so desperately needed.

Sources indicate that iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And in iOS 27.2, Apple introduced four more.

Per Apple’s release notes, here’s what’s upcoming:.

To get these fresh features, you’ll need to make sure your Shared Albums have been upgraded for iOS 27.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the problem with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software patch adds the following:.

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.

SynthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Users won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

In a recent development, A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, for Black Friday, it’s down to $179, which is the lowest price we've seen.

It has been revealed that bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

Industry observers note that as for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.
