By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 26, 2026 at 9:53AM EST.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

OMS Energy (OMSE +6.67%) reported a decrease in revenue for the first half of fiscal year 2027 but expanded its gross margin while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet with record cash reserves. Management attributed the revenue decline primarily to procurement delays in Saudi Arabia, where orders under a long-term supply agreement are being deferred instead of canceled. The organization is actively diversifying its geographic footprint with new orders in Malaysia, Kuwait, and Pakistan while shifting toward a higher-margin services revenue mix. Strategic efforts focus on cost discipline and cash generation to manage through extended customer decision cycles.

Operator: Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining OMS Energy Technologies, Inc.'s Earnings Presentation for the first half of fiscal year 2027. Today's presentation is being recorded. The company's financial and operating results for the 6 months ended September 30, 2026, have been released and are available on the OMS Investor Relations website at ir.omsos.com. Please note that today's discussion will contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements typically contain words such as may, will, expect, target, estimate, intend, believe, potential, continue, or similar expressions. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected or anticipated.

These include changes in customer spending and procurement, the timing of call-off orders and deliveries, geopolitical developments, supply chain conditions, and foreign exchange movements. Further information about risks is included in the firm's filings with the SEC. The company does not undertake any obligation to update forward-looking information, except as required under applicable law. Today's discussion also includes adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow, which are supplemental non-IFRS measures. Their definitions and reconciliations to the most directly comparable IFRS measures are included in the earnings release. I will now turn the presentation over to Mr. Meng Hock How. Please go ahead.

Recent findings suggest that meng Hock How: Thank you, operator, and thank you to everyone joining us today. I am Meng Hock How, CEO of OMS Energy Technologies. I'll discuss our first half performance, what we're seeing in customer orders and the progress we're making across our business. I will then address several questions that we expect investors to have about the results. For investors newer to OMS, we are Singapore headquartered equipment manufacturer and engineered solutions supplier serving upstream oil and gas operators. Our core products include Surface Wellhead and Christmas Tree Systems, Specialty Connectors and Pipe. We also provide premium threading, repair, and other engineering services through 11 manufacturing facilities across 6 markets in Asia Pacific, Middle East, and North Africa. Turning to our results.

I'm pleased to report that we expanded our gross margin, generated strong cash flow and further strengthened our debt-free balance sheet in the first half. Gross margin increased to 31.4% from 28.2% in the prior year period, and net profit margin improved to 18.8% from 17.6%. We generated $25.3 million in operating cash flow and approximately twice our net profit and ended September with a record $172.3 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash or approximately $4.06 per share. We delivered these results while macro conditions remain challenging given ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain disruption in our major markets. Our facilities remained operational throughout the period.

Customers continued to tender and place orders with OMS during the half, but took longer to commit and schedule deliveries, weighing on revenue. First half revenue was $66.7 million compared with $82.8 million a year ago, largely due to the slower pace of Saudi Aramco call-off orders. This was partially offset by increased activity in Malaysia and Thailand, showing the value of our diversified footprint. In the current environment, the challenge for OMS lies not in lack of opportunities, but in reduced visibility, extended decision cycle and execution timing. You will see that pattern throughout this period's result.

Industry observers note that with order timing harder to predict, we are concentrating on factors that we can control, including careful management of inventory, costs, and customer deliveries. By keeping inventory, purchasing and costs in line with the orders we actually received, we were able to protect profitability and generate strong cash flow despite fluctuating order volumes. Saudi Arabia is where reduced visibility and order timing have affected us most. Revenue from Specialty Connectors and Pipe was $37.1 million compared with $51.1 million a year ago as the timing of the order placed under our long-term supply agreement with Saudi Aramco continued to slow. I would like to emphasize, as previously mentioned, that these are deferred orders, not lost orders.

Our agreement with Saudi Aramco remains intact. Our relationship remains strong, and there has been no cancellation. To that end, we continue to receive business from Aramco. In September, we announced a $7.1 million order for specialty connectors and pipe won through an open tender outside our long-term agreement. Since that award, we have received a call-off order of approximately $3 million under the long-term agreement as well as a separate $500,000 order for loose connectors for Aramco's float equipment. We view these awards as a reflection of Aramco's confidence in our product and the delivery record we have built in the Kingdom over 15 years.

According to recent reports, in Indonesia, our operation in Bogor just received an order for specialty pipe and connectors valued at approximately $396,000 for Pertamina North West Java. This is a follow-on from the order we announced in January 2026. Furthermore, our operations in Singapore and Malaysia secured their first order for specialty connectors and pipe for Petronas in Malaysia, valued at approximately $687,000. Of that amount, $367,000 was delivered during the first half of fiscal 2027. We also continue to bid for supply contracts with Kuwait Oil Firm, KOC, and are actively engaged in the tender process we have entered after we qualified for the approved vendor list in July.

Recent findings suggest that also following that qualification, we received a $458,000 order from Tenaris for OMS connectors that we welded onto Tenaris pipe and supplied to Kuwait Oil Manufacturer as part of Tenaris OCTG package. While modest in size, the Petronas and Tenaris order extend our specialty connectors and pipe business to 2 more national oil companies, which we believe can lead to additional business over time. We've also recently bid to supply specialty connectors and Pipe for a development in the South China Sea with results expected next month. If we are successful, this will mark our reentry into China after more than 10 years and represent further progress in our ongoing geographic diversification efforts.

It has been revealed that in surface wellhead and Christmas trees, we continue to win orders while revenue follows customer and project schedules. First half revenue from Surface Wellhead and Christmas Tree was $3.5 million compared to $6.2 million a year ago. Indonesia is the main market for this business and upstream activities there has been slow over the past year as new oil and gas projects have taken longer to come online. In September, we revealed $2.3 million order from Pertamina Hulu Rokan under our existing 3-year supply contract following the contract extension we announced in March. We also recently received $766,000 order from Pertamina for choke valves, a component of Christmas tree systems.

It has been revealed that separately, we are awaiting a call-off of approximately $1 million from Pertamina under an existing contract. We also completed the stackup and function test of a upcoming compact surface wellhead and Christmas tree system for Pertamina, a milestone in developing our wellhead product offering with an established customer. The equipment has been delivered and is being installed by Pertamina on its Tamadun-001 field, where it is carrying out an unconventional drilling program. Indonesia holds vast unconventional oil and gas resources, including shale gas, coal-bed methane, methane hydrate, and shale oil, and commercial development is still at an early stage. We believe this installation position us well as that activity develops.

OMS Singapore has also just delivered a complete 10,000 psi wellhead and Christmas tree system to Orient Petroleum in Pakistan, marking OMS Singapore's first delivery of such a system to the country. Orient Petroleum is one of Pakistan's largest private exploration and production tech giant and has been operating since 1979. OMS Singapore has also received a supply contract for 2 sets of production tree for a Bleiswijk geothermal cluster in Netherlands. While the value is small at approximately $130,000, it is a step into the European energy sector that we want to build on. Across our service businesses, customers also continued to place orders during the half.

Other ancillary services revenue rose to $9.4 million from $7.5 million, an increase of approximately 25%, supported by repair, refurbishment, and engineering work in Thailand and Malaysia. This maintenance work depends less on new project approval than equipment sales do. Premium threading services revenue was $16.7 million compared to $18 million. Together, our services business accounted for approximately 39% of first half revenue, up from approximately 31% a year ago. In Singapore, we've also secured an approximately $0.55 million of repair work on production risers for a large oilfield services company for the upcoming Kikeh 3B Phase 2 subsea project in Malaysia. The Kikeh field is operated by PTTEP Malaysia. Our backlog reflects the period's slower order timing pattern.

In a recent development, at September 30, it stood at $40.9 million compared to $60.7 million at March 31, primarily due to call-off timing under the Saudi agreement. Our backlog comprises confirmed orders that have not yet been recognized as revenue and are expected to be delivered within the following 12 months. It does not include orders received after September 30, including the additional Saudi Aramco order I mentioned earlier. A framework agreement, a tender opportunity, and a confirmed call-off each represent different stages of the customer's procurement process and the backlog captures only the last of those stages. Today, opportunities are taking longer to move from tender to award and from framework agreement to call-off.

To put the backlog figure in context, Saudi Aramco maintained its 2026 capital spending guidance of $50 billion to $55 billion when it reported third quarter's results this month. Aramco attributed lower upstream spending in the quarter, mainly to the timing of crude oil increment projects and several of its major upstream developments, including the Dammam development and the second phase of Jafurah are scheduled to come on stream in 2027. Across the wider region, BMI expects oil and gas capital spending to grow about 4% this year and to average approximately 6% a year from 2027 to 2030. Now let me walk through our financial results in more detail.

First half revenue was $66.7 million compared to $82.8 million in the prior year period. Gross profit was $21 million compared to $23.3 million. Gross margin increased from 28.2% to 31.4%, supported by a more favorable mix in Saudi Specialty connectors and pipe and a greater contribution from higher-margin ancillary services in Thailand. Selling and general and administrative expenses were $7.1 million compared to $5.4 million in the prior year period. The increase primarily reflected personnel costs and professional services, governance, and compliance-related fees. Operating profit was $13.9 million compared to $17.9 million, and operating margin was 20.8% compared to 21.6%. Finance income increased to $2.4 million from $1.6 million, reflecting more cash placed in interest-earning deposits.

Industry observers note that income tax expense was $3.6 million compared with $4.6 million, and our effective tax rate was 22.3% compared to 24%. Net profit was $12.6 million compared with $14.6 million, and net profit margin increased to 18.8% from 17.6%. Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.28 compared with $0.33, reflecting lower profit attributable to shareholders and a higher weighted average share count. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million compared to $21.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin held relatively steady at 25.9% compared with 26.4% despite the 19% decline in revenue. We continue to use this supplement measure alongside the IFRS results. The earnings release sets out the adjustment and the reconciliation from net profit. Cash generation remained an area of strength.

Operating cash flow was $25.3 million compared with $26.4 million. Adjusted free cash flow was $19.9 million compared with $25.4 million. As described in our earnings release, this measure now deducts cash placed in fixed rate structured deposits, and the change from last year mainly reflects the $5 million we placed in these deposits during the period. Part of our cash generation came from a reduction in inventory, which contributed $9.5 million to operating cash flow compared to $12.2 million a year ago. Inventory ended September at $7.7 million compared to $17.2 million at March 31. The level of inventory and the timing of replenishment will affect cash flow as order activity changes.

We will continue to manage purchasing and production against the equipment needed for customer deliveries. Net cash used in investing activities was $5.4 million. This included $5 million placed in fixed rate structured deposits and approximately $0.4 million for property, plant, and equipment and software. These deposits are not included in our reported cash balance of $172.3 million. Cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash increased to a record $172.3 million at September 30 compared with $104.3 million at March 31. Our balance sheet remains free of bank borrowings. We continue to refine our capital allocation plan and assess investment opportunities while maintaining the financial flexibility to meet delivery commitments.

Looking ahead, our immediate planning reflects the slow pace of Saudi call-off and the orders we have in hand across the business. The September Aramco tender win and the Pertamina order were announced with expected delivery dates in January and March 2027, respectively. We are focused on execution against the schedule and continued engagement with our customers. We remain cautious about the timing of a wider recovery in procurement. At the same time, we are encouraged by our recent order activity, the growing contribution from our services business and the opportunities we are pursuing across the Middle East and Asia.

In a recent development, we have long-term agreement with leading national oil companies, 11 manufacturing facilities close to our customers and more than $172 million in cash with no debt. We believe this strength positions OMS well to capture future opportunities. Before we close, I would like to address questions investors are likely to have in the half, including how current visibility compares with the expectation that we discussed in June. Question one, how much of the earnings decline is attributable to geopolitical tensions and have projects been canceled? We have not observed material projects cancellation directly attributable to geopolitical development. The effect has been indirect primarily through longer customer decision cycle, deferred projects award and increased caution in customer capital spending decisions.

For OMS, the main operating problem has been the slower pace of Saudi call-off orders. Some customers have taken longer to finalize investment decisions or have adjusted project time lines, and it is difficult to isolate a specific financial impact. Opportunities remain in place, but decision and awards are taking longer. We are actively pursuing work in Malaysia, Indonesia, the UAE, Kuwait and China. Question two, is demand weakening, particularly in the Middle East? We would characterize the environment as one of increased caution rather than broad-based demand weakness. Activity levels vary by customers and markets. Customers continue to evaluate opportunities and pursue strategic projects, although decision-making and approval processes have become more measured.

In certain cases, this has translated into longer approval and procurement cycles. For OMS, that highlights up as a slower Saudi call-off and a longer gap between tender and award. Several of the largest oilfield services have also pointed to the limited near-term visibility in the Middle East in their recent results. Even so, Saudi Aramco has maintained its 2026 capital spending guidance and has continued to award us business, including the $7.1 million tender award in September and additional orders since then. Our focus remains on supporting customers while adapting to changing market conditions. Third question, have supply chain disruption become a major concern? Supply chain conditions remain manageable, but less predictable than in previous period.

We have experienced longer lead time and occasional logistic challenges affecting certain projects. Management continues to work closely with suppliers and customers to mitigate these impacts where possible. The fourth question, how are margins holding up? And can they be sustained? Well, first half gross margin increased to 31.4% from 28.2%, supported by the mix of equipment specification and services. Operating margin was 20.8%. We continue to manage procurement, project execution and operating costs carefully. Our priority is maintaining financial discipline while remaining competitive in the markets we serve. However, if activity slows further in the second half, margins could be affected. We will continue to manage costs carefully as conditions evolve.

In a recent development, question five, do we expect conditions to improve in the second half? Given the uncertain geopolitical and macroeconomic environment, we do not believe it will be appropriate to speculate on the timing or extent of any improvement. Customers continue to tender and place orders with OMS. Improvement depends on visibility returning and decision cycles shortening, and we do not control that timing. Continued uncertainty could further influence customer spending, project timing and supply chain performance. We continue to maintain long-standing customer relationships, technical capabilities and a diversified market presence. Management remains focused on factors within our control, including customer engagement, operational execution, cost management, and cash generation.

According to recent reports, sixth question is, does the expectation of modest FY 2027 revenue growth discussed in June still hold? Well, in June, we expected fiscal 2027 revenue to be modestly above fiscal 2026, assuming no further material geopolitical disruption. Since then, the Saudi call-off activity has remained slow and the timing of a broader pickup remains uncertain. Given the first half revenue of $66.7 million and the continued slow pace of call-off, we no longer expect fiscal 2027 revenue to exceed fiscal 2026. We're not providing a specific range today, and we will revision investors as visibility on order timing improves. The last point or question 7, how do you plan to use your cash?

Well, our priorities are consistent with what we shared in June. First, we are reinvesting in core businesses, including capacity, certification, and in-region capabilities that support our growth. Second, we continue to review bolt-on acquisition opportunities with discipline and our cash position allows us to pursue them without raising new capital or taking on debt. We do not right now have a dividend and buyback program in place, but our balance sheet gives us the flexibility to introduce one when timing and conditions are right. We continue to refine our capital allocation plan, and we'll upgrade investors as it develops. With this, we conclude our prepared remarks. Thank you very much for joining us today.

In a recent development, operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you all for participating. You may now disconnect your lines. Thank you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has quietly revealed the upcoming opening of its latest retail store in Hyderabad, India. Located at the Lakeshore Mall in Kukatpally, it opens at 5pm on Thursday, December 10.

As is now usual, the organization has created some exclusive wallpaper to mark the event, and you can download it for iPhone, iPad, and Mac ….

The store will be the seventh one to open in India. There’s no press release or photos as yet – the firm has simply quietly added the store to its list in the country.

According to recent reports, as we’ve previously explained, Apple had been trying to open retail stores in India since at least 2015, but had to undertake a lengthy battle with the government before finally being allowed to do so in 2023. Since then, the tech giant has averaged two newly introduced stores a year.

India has taken a clever approach to economic development, offering both incentives to establish local manufacturing plants, and barriers to imports of foreign-made products. That carrot-and-stick approach has proven successful, with companies like Apple jumping through the necessary hoops in order to sell their products to the second largest population in the world.

It has been revealed that an India First initiative required companies to manufacture a significant proportion of their products within the country in order to avoid high import tariffs. This forced Apple, Samsung, and other companies to establish manufacturing plants in India, bringing jobs to the country.

It has been revealed that additionally, India does not allow company-branded retail stores unless the same conditions are met. That particular requirement was mostly intended to target Apple.

The proposal worked, with Apple asking its suppliers and iPhone assemblers to establish manufacturing plants within India. Initially, that was just for the iPhone SE, but more advanced phones have gradually been added, and today the country is the second largest manufacturing base after China. All iPhones sold in the US are made in India.

Apple has for some time now created unique wallpapers to mark the opening of each latest store, and the latest example is particularly beautiful.

To download it, you need to visit this page on the device for which you want to use it. For example, if you visit the page on a Mac, you will automatically be taken to the desktop version.

#131253. The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season

The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.
  • Sources indicate that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one.
  • For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

Sources indicate that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.).

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

In a recent development, the iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s mentioned they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV reveals on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

It has been revealed that the iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

Sources indicate that the Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

Recent findings suggest that multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

Sources indicate that for the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

Sources indicate that it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

In a recent development, the Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Recent findings suggest that some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

Sources indicate that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

According to recent reports, for most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

#131252. CTO of 'RansomwareHelp' Indicted for Wire Fraud

CTO of 'RansomwareHelp' Indicted for Wire Fraud

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Krebsonsecurity

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use “advanced cryptographic tools” to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the organization was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.
  • A portion of the now-defunct website ransomwarehelp.com.
  • The website RansomwareHelp urged victims “Do not pay the ransom!,” claiming its advanced cryptographic tools could restore 100 percent of data, servers, and systems to their original format, and that there was no need to give in to extortion demands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use “advanced cryptographic tools” to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the organization was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

A portion of the now-defunct website ransomwarehelp.com.

The website RansomwareHelp urged victims “Do not pay the ransom!,” claiming its advanced cryptographic tools could restore 100 percent of data, servers, and systems to their original format, and that there was no need to give in to extortion demands.

“Our cryptography experts use proprietary tools and algorithms to achieve 100% data recovery, all backed by a success rate of over 99%,” the website enthused, claiming the tech giant had over 28 years of experience and a team of 80 experts in cryptography, cybersecurity, forensic analysis and reverse engineering. “We never promote, intermediate or pay ransom to threat actors on behalf of our clients.”.

But according to an indictment (PDF) returned this week in Rhode Island, the company’s co-founder — 52-year-old Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar of Miami and Medellin, Colombia — routinely paid ransomware groups for a decryption key to unlock victim data, and then charged those victims well above what he’d secretly paid the threat actors [Palacio’s indictment was reported earlier this week by 404 Media, but for some reason that story did not name the defendant’s company].

Industry observers note that the indictment claims the FBI set up a sting operation in which the feds were posing both as a ransomware victim firm and as a fictitious ransomware group. Pretending to be victims of a cyberattack, investigators contacted RansomwareHelp and supplied the company with a copy of a phony ransomware note, saying they did not wish to pay a ransom. RansomwareHelp replied by reiterating its policy against negotiating with or making ransom payments to threat actors.

The government said Palacio soon after contacted the fake ransomware group run by the FBI and requested the lowest possible price for the decryptor. FBI investigators responded with a price of .2 bitcoin, or around $13,000 at the time. Less than 48 hours later, Palacio allegedly told agents acting as the victim company that the diagnostic assessment was successful and that the cost of decrypting the files would be $13,260.

Industry observers note that the following day, the government alleges, Palacio messaged the fictitious ransomware group operated by the feds and asked to reduce the ransom demand to $4,000 for the purchase of a decryption tool. The indictment states that the agreed upon price was around $6,000 in bitcoin, and that Palacio charged the FBI’s fake victim firm $16,010, including an initial $2,750 diagnostic fee and the full fee of $13,260.

Paul Ihme is co-founder of the security firm Soteria. Ihme told KrebsOnSecurity that in 2024 he heard from a small accounting firm that had paid RansomwareHelp a diagnostic fee to help recover from a Lockbit ransomware infection that had locked all of their manufacturer and client data.

Ihme stated RansomwareHelp sent a proposal to the victim with a recovery price of $438,880, which it claimed included “professional configuration of forensic servers,” “expert engineering hours of programming to configure decryption algorithms,” and “eight (6-hour processing cycles) related to the decryption process.”.

A portion of the proposal that RansomwareHelp sent to a victim accounting firm in March 2024. Click to enlarge.

The proposal stated that the recovery process involved reverse engineering the ransomware encryption using “510 preconfigured forensic servers of the maximum quantitative capacity located in different parts of the world.”.

“Our programmers will inject randomly the encryption codes extracted during the forensic and cryptographic analysis using brute force processes,” the proposal claimed.

It has been revealed that ihme said RansomwareHelp insisted that they be allowed unrestricted remote access into the victim’s network to run their diagnostic checks and analyses, using an Anydesk remote desktop software installer. Ihme believes RansomwareHelp insisted on that remote access in part so that the manufacturer could delete all copies of the ransomware notes left by the attackers on the victim’s network.

Sources indicate that A typical ransomware note is a plain text file that introduces the ransomware group and lays out their demands, and it includes a way to contact them — often an email address or a live chat session on a darknet website. In most cases, the attackers will leave a copy of the ransom note on every system on the victim network that gets locked.

In a recent development, but Ihme remarked a review of the company’s network at the time found only one copy of the ransom note, which was unearthed from a backup snapshot on one of the infected computers. When they connected to the Lockbit chat server with the provided user ID, they discovered that someone had already been negotiating with the Lockbit extortionists for several days.

A screenshot of a 2024 conversation between Lockbit and RansomwareHelp, which was secretly negotiating with the extortion group. Click to enlarge.

“The charitable view would be to say that they were using Anydesk so they could grab the stuff they needed without having to walk the client through downloading and uploading a bunch of stuff,” Ihme said. “A legitimate firm would say, ‘Hey, send us a copy of the ransom note,’ which will have a link or URL to go to and chat with the threat actors. What they were doing is using that access to delete ransomware notes off the systems. The only reason they would do that is to prevent the victim from jumping into that chat itself.”.

Indeed, RansomwareHelp pleaded with the Lockbit group throughout the chat not to reveal to the victim that they were negotiating. However, Lockbit swiftly grew annoyed with the length of the negotiations, replying that the victims had waited too long and that the ransom demand would increase by $100,000 for every day they dithered further.

It has been revealed that the Lockbit representative starts raising the ransom demand after multiple negotiators begin interacting with the threat actors. Click to enlarge.

In the end, the accounting firm took Ihme’s advice and went with a more established security firm that helped them negotiate a payment to Lockbit.

“The victim told us, ‘If we don’t get this data back, our business is over’,” Ihme recalled. “They ended up paying half of what RansomwareHelp was going to charge them.”.

The chats show RansomwareHelp kept pestering Lockbit to negotiate a deal even after it was clear a upcoming negotiator was engaging with the ransomware group on the victim’s behalf.

Industry observers note that “I tell you something, that person who is negotiating with you for the other chat is damaging the whole process,” RansomwareHelp wrote to Lockbit. “Please do not change the price. I am doing my best to achieve it.”.

Ihme mentioned RansomwareHelp primarily targeted small to medium sized businesses that weren’t particularly tech-savvy, noting that many of the technical claims made on the organization’s website and in their proposal are patently farcical. For example, the proposal sent to the accounting firm said it could break six types of encryption, and then proceeded to list a number of irrelevant password hashing algorithms like SHA-256.

According to recent reports, “If it were really true these guys could decrypt any ransomware out there, this guy would be a billionaire,” Ihme said. “They were going after people who don’t have any technical knowledge, are desperate, and don’t have anyone advising them about how any of this stuff works.”.

Sources indicate that the case against Palacio marks the latest in a string of recent prosecutions by the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) targeting security firms alleged to have conspired with fraudsters to defraud clients. In early October, the government charged 54-year-old Edward Dubrovsky, an executive at the Canadian cybersecurity firm Cybersteward. The government has sealed the case against Dubrovsky, but he is currently facing cyber extortion and conspiracy charges.

Around the same time as Dubrovsky’s arrest, the DoJ charged MonsterCloud CEO Zohar Pinhasi, 50, with wire fraud and conspiracy for allegedly charging customers to remediate ransomware attacks without paying the hackers. According to charging documents, Pinhasi secretly went behind his customers’ backs and paid hackers anyway, paying ransomware groups $8 million while charging customers $19 million.

In a recent development, in July, Angelo Martino, a 41-year-old ransomware negotiator from Land O’Lakes, Florida, was sentenced to 70 months in prison for conspiring with the Blackcat/ALPHV ransomware group to extort multiple victims. According to the DoJ, Martino was paid by BlackCat attackers to provide confidential information about the negotiating position and strategy of his employer’s clients and enable the ransomware actors to maximize the ransoms paid by the victims.

5 upcoming Apple Health features you should try in iOS 27.3 – if your phone qualifies

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3.
  • Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.
  • Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

Recent findings suggest that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

It has been revealed that A upcoming feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a upcoming feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

The latest app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

It has been revealed that normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the latest Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Recent findings suggest that some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone owners. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.
